ServoEx wraps the SDK servo with a cleaner API.

Instead of calling servo.setPosition() on the raw SDK object, you use servo.set(value) on the ServoEx. The value maps across the servo's configured range.

Import from com.seattlesolvers.solverslib.hardware.servos.

Declare a private ServoEx field. In initialize(), create it with: servo = new ServoEx(hardwareMap, "back_servo").

That's it — no range needed. The default ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, same as the raw SDK servo.

servo.set(0.5) sends the servo to its middle position.

If you want a custom range, you can pass min and max in the constructor or call servo.setRange(min, max) later.

Schedule an InstantCommand that calls servo.set(1.0).

The servo moves to its maximum position and holds there.

servo.set(0.0) goes to minimum. servo.set(0.5) centers it.

ServoEx handles the math — just give it a value in the configured range.

Create a SequentialCommandGroup that sweeps the servo: InstantCommand(servo.set(0.0)), WaitCommand(1000), InstantCommand(servo.set(0.5)), WaitCommand(1000), InstantCommand(servo.set(1.0)), WaitCommand(1000), InstantCommand(servo.set(0.0)).

Schedule it.

The servo moves through min, middle, max, and back — with 1-second pauses.

servo.setPwm(pwmRange) configures custom pulse width limits for specialty servos.

servo.setInverted(true) reverses direction.

servo.getRawPosition() returns the raw 0.0-1.0 position.

servo.getServo() gives the underlying SDK Servo object.

servo.setCachingTolerance(0.01) enables power caching.

For continuous rotation servos, use CRServo and CRServoEx from the same package.
